name: Pixel collage
source: A short manifesto on an off-white paper ground in which ONE ring of matching 16-bit pixel icons (heart, camera, vinyl, book, cat, plant, coin, cap, gamepad) is the actor: it orbits, is struck by ink smears and handwriting, breaks apart, and its members stand in for words and for the letters of LOVE, alongside a few cut-out photos graded in one hot gradient map. Tiny type, a handwritten signature, ink and pixel dissolves. Described from a frame strip; no files or pixels are carried.

frame_device.what: A paper ground with a soft vignette and no grain, and ONE cohesive set of about 12 to 16 pixel-art icons drawn by the art department in one style (same grid, same outline, same palette). The icons are the frame device: a ring at the centre that orbits like a clock face, and the stage on which each word is said by one object. Tiny sans type and a handwritten pen line are the only text.
frame_device.moves: The ring orbits slowly; ink strokes and brush smears strike it and knock members out one at a time, each flashing; one icon at a time steps forward as the beat's verb or noun, then hands the stage back to the ring. The pen that writes a line is also the cursor that scatters the objects.

ground_motion: The paper drifts a few percent in tone toward a warm tint and back over 8 to 10 s, the vignette breathes with it, and the ring keeps its slow orbit between strikes, so the stage lives while one icon speaks.

type.classes: One small clean sans (14 to 28 px on a 1080 frame) for the spoken line, sentence case, with a large pixel or heavy word only where one word is the beat; a handwritten single-stroke script (the signature, the question) drawn from Hershey paths.
type.behaviour: Lines are written word by word by a pen that runs ahead of the text (draw-on), or typed with a blinking cursor beside the icon that says them; a word may be swapped in place while the rest holds. Small type is always fully readable at rest, inside the safe area, never cropped.

image.treatment: Pixel-art icons in one set (generated as one style by the art department, never mixed with vector or photo icons), and cut-out photographs (a head, a hand) run through ONE hot gradient map (orange to red to black) so they read as the same material. Ink smears, brush swirls and scribbles are the only organic marks.
image.behaviour: Icons are stepped objects: they move on twos (12 fps), squash on landing and may smear on a fast move; photos enter as cut-outs, never as rectangles, and dissolve into pixels. Nothing is a stock picture.

transitions: ink smear transition (a brush smear sweeps the frame and the next scene is under it)
pixel dissolve (the image breaks into its own pixels and the next object assembles from them)
icon-ring handoff (the next object is the ring member that was just struck)
colour flare then ground change (cyan or red wash to black, then back to paper)
scribble out (a dense ball of strokes swallows the letters)

techniques.name: Ink smear transition
techniques.what: A black brush smear sweeps across the frame, turns the page, and the next scene is already there under it.
techniques.route: RasanShape.ink(tl, wipeEl, {at, duration: 0.5, mode: "smear"}) over a full-frame ink layer (an SVG blob path or a cut-out brush PNG from art/assets); the incoming scene sits beneath at opacity 1 and is revealed as the smear clears; outgoing content scales 1 to 1.04 and smears (RasanShape.smear) as it is struck.

techniques.name: Icon ring orbit
techniques.what: A circle of matching pixel icons orbits like a clock face, a brush stroke strikes one at a time and it flashes.
techniques.route: 12 to 16 icon elements placed on a circle (radius 28% of the short side) in a rotating wrapper; wrapper rotation 0 to 360 over the scene (ease none) and each icon counter-rotates so it stays upright; a strike is a 0.12 s scale 1 to 1.25 (back.out) with a 0.2 s accent flash behind, then a 3 to 8% overshoot settle; RasanShape.stepped(tl, {fps: 12}) on the ring scene.

techniques.name: Signature draw-on
techniques.what: A handwritten line or signature draws itself, a pen tip running ahead of the stroke.
techniques.route: art.mjs hand --text "..." --out art/assets/sig.svg (Hershey single-stroke paths, one path per stroke); RasanShape.drawOn(tl, svg, {at, duration: 1.2, stagger: 0.04, ease: "power1.inOut"}); a small pen-tip circle follows the head with RasanShape.followPath(tl, pen, headPath, {at, duration: 1.2}).

techniques.name: Gradient-mapped cut-out
techniques.what: A cut-out photo (a head in profile, a rising hand) in one hot colour ramp, standing in as the speaker.
techniques.route: art.mjs cutout then art.mjs treat --op gradient-map --colors <dark>,<accent>,<hot>; the PNG slides in from the edge (x 120 to 0, 0.6 s power3.out) with a 12% squash on arrival (RasanShape.squash) and dissolves out as pixels (RasanShape.dissolve mode "pixel", cell 8 to 24).

techniques.name: Letters scatter and settle
techniques.what: A word falls apart into its letters, which tumble apart and settle as tiny glyphs, or an icon takes a letter's place and the real letter replaces it.
techniques.route: RasanShape.split(el, {by: "chars"}); RasanShape.scatter(tl, spans, {at, from: "random-seeded", seed: 7, settle: 0.6}); for LOVE put a pixel icon in each letter slot in turn (0.3 s each, flipping the ground white, black, red), then swap to the real glyph.

techniques.name: Stepped on twos
techniques.what: The whole scene moves at 12 fps, like hand-drawn animation, so pixel art reads as animated pixel art.
techniques.route: RasanShape.stepped(tl, {fps: 12}) on the scene's timeline (8 fps for a held-down beat); every tween keeps a real ease underneath, the quantisation is the style; type and the camera stay smooth by living on a second timeline.

techniques.name: An object says the word
techniques.what: One icon takes the stage as the beat's verb (the camera is "action", the book is "intention", the vinyl is "curiosity") and the word types beside it.
techniques.route: Icon scale 0 to 1 with back.out(1.7) and 6% overshoot after a 0.1 s anticipation dip (scale 0.92); a starburst or ribbon swoosh behind it draws on (RasanShape.drawOn); the word types with a blinking cursor at 14 cps, then the object exits along the ribbon, which is the next transition.

techniques.name: Word swap in place
techniques.what: A line holds while one word is replaced where it stands ("you dont." becomes "you just show it."), so the line is the one thing that never leaves.
techniques.route: Fixed words are a still span; the changing word is its own span in the same slot: out y 0 to -10 and opacity 1 to 0 (0.2 s power2.in), in y 12 to 0 with a 4 px settle (0.4 s back.out(1.4)); the line's width follows with a 0.3 s power3.inOut tween of the span's width so nothing jumps.

techniques.name: Ink break
techniques.what: The ring spins up, brush swirls knock the objects off it and some turn into black ink blobs while others fly out, leaving the stage almost empty.
techniques.route: Each icon gets a seeded outward vector (RasanShape.scatter from: "radius"); on strike it squashes 20% against the swirl direction (RasanShape.squash), smears 2 frames (RasanShape.smear) and either flies out or its pixels become a black blob (RasanShape.dissolve mode "pixel" into an ink-coloured fill); the swirl itself is RasanShape.ink mode "blot" over 0.6 s.

techniques.name: Scribble out
techniques.what: A tangle of black strokes and red loops swallows the letters into a dense ball, and the film ends on the scribble.
techniques.route: A hand-drawn scribble SVG (art.mjs trace --lineart of a drawn scribble, or art.mjs hand with the scribble font) drawn on with RasanShape.drawOn(tl, svg, {at, duration: 1.0, stagger: 0.02, ease: "none"}) over the drifted letters; the last stroke lands on the final beat and the frame holds still for 0.6 s.

techniques.name: Colour flare and wash
techniques.what: A cyan flare swells from one edge, the page washes red, then black, as the register changes from question to answer.
techniques.route: A full-frame gradient div (radial, accent to transparent) scales 0.2 to 2.4 from the left edge over 0.5 s power2.inOut while the ground tweens paper to the wash colour (0.4 s) and the type colour inverts in sync; this is a palette move, no blur and no glow.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of a line enters from its own place (its own offset, scale and blur) and settles into the line with a gentle lift, the key word last with a little more overshoot; type-on only where a pen or a cursor is the show.
techniques.route: RasanShape.split(el, {by: "words"}); GSAP from each word's own x/y offset (24 to 80 px, different per word), scale 0.88 to 1.15 and blur 6 to 12 px to rest, 0.55 s, stagger 0.09 s; end with a 4 to 8 px lift settling back (y -6 to 0) on back.out(1.4); every word readable at rest and the line whole before the next line starts; the next line's first word starts 0.2 s before this line's last settles.

signature: One ring of matching pixel objects speaks the whole film: it orbits, is struck by ink, breaks apart, and its members take the place of the letters of the last word before they scatter and are scribbled out.

density.note: A new object, a stroke or a swap every 0.8 to 1.5 s; stepped on twos, with the ring orbiting between strikes. Layers per shot at the peak: 5 to 10 (ground, vignette, ring, one icon, ink, pen line, tiny type, flare).

palette.ground: off-white paper (#EFEDE6) with a soft vignette
palette.ink: near black (#111) for type and brush, with black grounds for spoken words
palette.accent: one hot red-orange (#E8421E), with a cyan flare used once
palette.note: A brand palette overrides these; the devices stay. The accent is also the gradient-map's hot end.

do: Generate ONE icon set in ONE pixel style and use only it
Run every photo through the same gradient map
Let the pen that writes a line also be the cursor that strikes the objects
Step the pixel scenes on twos and keep type smooth
Squash, smear and overshoot the objects (character motion language)
Keep 5 to 10 independently timed layers at the peak of a shot
dont: Do not mix pixel icons with vector or photo icons
Do not use stock photos, ungraded, as rectangles
Do not add grain, glow or 3D (this grammar is flat paper and pixels)
Do not crop or hide the small type
Do not repeat a technique on consecutive beats
Do not let an ink smear hide the line that is being read
fits: explainer for an idea or a feeling
launch ladder (each rung an object says its word)
